questions.q: Why does the online-order path use a Fabric Eventstream instead of a nightly batch job?
options: Online orders arrive continuously all day, and an Eventstream is built to receive and route continuous event traffic in near real time
Eventstreams are required for all data ingestion regardless of source
Batch jobs cannot technically read JSON payloads
The nightly POS export path also uses an Eventstream
questions.explain: Fabric & Real-Time Analytics Lesson 19's Eventstream is designed for continuous event ingestion, matching how online orders actually arrive.

questions.q: What is bronze's job in this design, per Databricks & Delta Lake Lesson 26?
options: Preserve the raw event faithfully, untransformed, so a downstream bug can always be replayed from an unmodified source
Apply business logic and produce the final aggregated tables
Store only online order data, never POS exports
Deduplicate and clean all data before it lands
questions.explain: Bronze lands data as-is; cleaning and business logic happen in later layers, not at ingestion.

questions.q: Why does this design target at-least-once delivery with idempotent landing, rather than building exactly-once delivery end to end?
options: Exactly-once end-to-end is expensive and usually unnecessary; keying landed rows on the source event ID lets a redelivered event overwrite instead of duplicate
At-least-once delivery is impossible to make idempotent
Exactly-once delivery is the only guarantee Fabric Eventstreams support
Delivery guarantees don't matter for this project since data loss is acceptable
questions.explain: Lesson 12 frames exactly-once vs. at-least-once as a trade-off; idempotent landing (via MERGE on event_id) makes at-least-once safe without the cost of true exactly-once.

questions.q: What tool handles the nightly POS export path, and why?
options: Databricks Autoloader, because it picks up only new files incrementally rather than re-scanning the whole export folder each run
A Fabric Eventstream, the same tool used for online orders
A manual script run once at the end of each quarter
Autoloader is not used anywhere in this design
questions.explain: Autoloader (Databricks & Delta Lake Lesson 32) is built for incremental file ingestion, matching the nightly-export pattern.

questions.q: What concrete freshness SLA does this lesson land on, replacing the vague "same-day" requirement?
options: Online sales visible within minutes of the Eventstream receiving them; in-store sales visible by the next morning after the nightly export
All data, online and in-store, must be visible within one second
No freshness number is defined — "same-day" remains the working requirement
In-store sales are visible instantly; online sales are delayed by a week
questions.explain: The hybrid ingestion design makes the real freshness numbers concrete: near-real-time for streaming online orders, next-morning for the nightly batch.
